title: Active management graduation rule becomes risk-adjusted: an in-trade action class passes if it gives up <= a pre-stated R/trade (0.05R proposed) while cutting book max drawdown or worst-5% outcome materially (>=15%), across folds, vs a random-intervention control, measured on the whole book; then pre-register the break-even-stop-after-peak test on the real-money legs under it
note: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-10-29 ~06:25Z (popup, verbatim answer): "Small R cost for big risk cut (Recommended)". Option text shown: 'Passes if it gives up at most a set amount of R per trade (I'd propose 0.05R, fixed before the run) while cutting the book's max drawdown or worst 5% of outcomes materially (e.g. 15%+). Must hold across time periods and beat a random-intervention control, measured on the whole book.' Operator reasoning, verbatim: "if we've gotten to a place where we can still find ourselves getting reward while zeroing out the risk of the trade, then that seems to me like it's a better trading decision overall than to keep on time and time again just giving back all of the gains." Supersedes the 'judged against hold' (mean net R) wording of docs/ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL.md § Active management clause 4 for graduation. Unchanged: each class graduates on its OWN registered test; net of the full cost stack; rule registered before the run; Tier-3/mandate path to execute; two gates; TP doctrine. Motivating case: ADA-AM-CASE (break-even stop: EV cost 0.01-0.03R, worst -1.04R -> -0.17R, sub-floor n=19).
